bugs.what: lcs.align breaks LCS ties toward insertion (strict >), so ambiguous alignments differ from SPEC 2.3
hunks.group_blocks merges blocks only when the gap is < 2N (SPEC 3.2: <= 2N); masked behind lcs-tiebreak in the visible examples
parser.parse_range ignores the t,0 rule (SPEC 6.6): an empty range gets position t-1, so insertions land a line early / creation reports offset 1 / .rej and stat show t-1,0

applier.apply_hunks assigns shift instead of accumulating it (SPEC 7.2): from the third hunk on, base/expected ignore earlier hunks' line-count changes -> spurious/wrong offsets, wrong FAILED lines, misplaced context-free insertions
edits:
ldiff/applier.py
        shift = added - len(hunk.old_lines())
        shift += added - len(hunk.old_lines())

bugs.what: locate.fuzz_window computes the trailing ignore count from the leading context (SPEC 7.4); only shows with fuzz on hunks whose leading and trailing context differ (near the file edges): dropped changes or rejects
edits:
ldiff/locate.py
    trail = min(fuzz, hunk.leading_context())
    trail = min(fuzz, hunk.trailing_context())

bugs.what: text.split_lines uses str.splitlines(True): form feed, vertical tab, lone CR, U+2028... also end lines (SPEC 1.2: only \n does); CRLF still works, but files with ^L/\v/lone \r are mis-split, diffs show phantom lines and patched files get extra newlines
locate.candidates sorts by distance only; the stable sort puts the earlier position first at equal distance (SPEC 7.5: later first) -> hunks land on the wrong copy of repeated blocks
parser.label_of takes the first whitespace-separated field (SPEC 6.2: up to the first TAB): labels with spaces are cut -> wrong file from -p, wrong .rej headers and stat label lines
edits:
ldiff/parser.py
    fields = line[4:].split(None, 1)
    return fields[0] if fields else ""
    return line[4:].split("\t", 1)[0]

bugs.what: cli passes `opts.fuzz or DEFAULT_FUZZ`, so -F 0 means fuzz 2 (SPEC 8.2): hunks that need fuzz succeed instead of being rejected
